title: 2012 HMMT February Guts Problem 16
statement: Let \(A, B, C\), and \(D\) be points randomly selected independently and uniformly within the unit square. What is the probability that the six lines \(\overline{A B}, \overline{A C}, \overline{A D}, \overline{B C}, \overline{B D}\), and \(\overline{C D}\) all have positive slope?

solutions.text: \(\frac{1}{24}\) Consider the sets of \(x\)-coordinates and \(y\)-coordinates of the points. In order to make 6 lines of positive slope, we must have smallest \(x\)-coordinate must be paired with the smallest \(y\)-coordinate, the second smallest together, and so forth. If we fix the order of the \(x\)-coordinates, the probability that the corresponding \(y\)-coordinates are in the same order is \(1 / 24\).
